stem: A park has a grassy mound with the same cross-section all the way across. The cross-section is modelled by \[h(x) = -0.0004x^{3} + 0.024x^{2}, \quad 0 \le x \le 60,\] where \(x\) metres is the horizontal distance from one edge of the mound and \(h\) metres is the height of the ground, as shown in the diagram.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the mound meets the ground again at \(x = 60\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find \(h'(x)\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the highest point of the mound.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the gradient of the mound at \(x = 10\), and the angle the slope makes with the horizontal there.

parts.label: e
parts.text: On the way up, the mound is steepest where \(h'(x)\) is greatest. Find the value of \(x\) at this point and the gradient there.

parts.label: f
parts.text: A straight plank is laid as the tangent to the mound at \(x = 50\). Find the equation of this tangent, and the value of \(x\) where the plank reaches the ground. The ground is level beyond \(x = 60\).

parts.label: g
parts.text: Find the area of the cross-section of the mound.

parts.label: h
parts.text: The mound is 25 m long, measured at right angles to the cross-section. Find the volume of soil in the mound.

idea: One function carries the whole question. Derivatives give gradients, the highest point and the steepest point; the integral gives the area of the cross-section, and the volume of a shape with a constant cross-section is that area times the width.

solution.label: c
steps: \(h(40) = -25.6 + 38.4 = 12.8\). The gradient is positive before \(x = 40\) and negative after it, so this is the highest point.

solution.label: e
steps: The rate of change of \(h'(x)\) is \(-0.0024x + 0.048\), which is zero at \(x = 20\). (The calculator's maximum of the graph of \(h'\) gives the same.)

solution.label: f
steps: The plank reaches the ground where \(-0.6x + 40 = 0\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find \(f'(x)\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the two stationary points of the graph of \(f\), and state the nature of each.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Sketch the graph of \(f\) for \(0 \le x \le 4\). Label the stationary points and the two end points with their coordinates.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the values of \(k\) for which the equation \(f(x) = k\) has three solutions with \(0 \le x \le 4\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x = 2\).

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the area of the region between the graph of \(f\) and the \(x\)-axis, for \(0 \le x \le 4\).

parts.label: g
parts.text: Show that the triangle formed by the tangent in part (e) and the two coordinate axes has the same area as the region in part (f).

idea: The stationary points and the end points fix the shape of the graph. A horizontal line \(y = k\) meets the graph three times only if it lies strictly between the minimum and the maximum, and does not go above or below the end points.

solution.label: b
solution.answer: \((1, 4)\) is a local maximum and \((3, 2)\) is a local minimum

solution.label: c
solution.answer: A curve from \((0, 2)\) up to \((1, 4)\), down to \((3, 2)\) and up to \((4, 4)\)

solution.label: d
steps: The graph goes 2 up to 4, down to 2, up to 4. A line \(y = k\) with \(2 < k < 4\) crosses each of the three pieces once.
At \(k = 2\) or \(k = 4\) there are only two solutions (for example \(k = 4\) gives \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\)).

solution.label: f
steps: The graph is above the \(x\)-axis for \(0 \le x \le 4\) (its lowest value is 2).

solution.label: g
steps: The tangent meets the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 6)\) and the \(x\)-axis where \(-1.5x + 6 = 0\), at \((4, 0)\).

stem: A chocolate company sells its bars in a closed cardboard box in the shape of a triangular prism. Each end of the box is an equilateral triangle with sides of \(x\) cm, and the box is \(l\) cm long, as shown in the diagram. The box must hold 500 cm\(^{3}\).

stem.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 306 229" width="306" height="229" role="img" aria-label="A box in the shape of a triangular prism. Each end is an equilateral triangle with sides of x cm. The length of the box, from one triangular end to the other, is l cm."><path d="M45.2 183.7 L149.2 183.7 L97.2 93.7 Z" fill="#eaf0fb" stroke="none" stroke-width="0" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M149.2 183.7 L245.3 119.7 L193.3 29.6 L97.2 93.7 Z" fill="#dde6f6" stroke="none" stroke-width="0" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="M45.2 183.7 L149.2 183.7" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="2.0" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M149.2 183.7 L97.2 93.7" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="2.0" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M97.2 93.7 L45.2 183.7" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="2.0" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M149.2 183.7 L245.3 119.7" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="2.0" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M97.2 93.7 L193.3 29.6" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="2.0" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M245.3 119.7 L193.3 29.6" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="2.0" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round"/><path d="M45.2 183.7 L141.3 119.7" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="1.2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><path d="M141.3 119.7 L245.3 119.7" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="1.2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><path d="M141.3 119.7 L193.3 29.6" stroke="#0b0d12" stroke-width="1.2" fill="none" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/><text x="97.2" y="202.8" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-family="'Times New Roman', Times, serif" fill="#0b0d12" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round">x</text><text x="59.2" y="143.8" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-family="'Times New Roman', Times, serif" fill="#0b0d12" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round">x</text><text x="209.2" y="164.8" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-family="'Times New Roman', Times, serif" fill="#0b0d12" paint-order="stroke" stroke="#fff" stroke-width="3" stroke-linejoin="round">l</text></svg>

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the area of one triangular end is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}x^{2}\) cm\(^{2}\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that \(l = \dfrac{2000}{\sqrt{3}\,x^{2}}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Show that the total area of card, \(A\) cm\(^{2}\), is given by \(A = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}x^{2} + \dfrac{6000}{\sqrt{3}\,x}\).

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}x}\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Find the value of \(x\) that uses the least card, and the length \(l\) of this box.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the least area of card.

parts.label: g
parts.text: The marketing team wants a longer box, 20 cm long, that still holds 500 cm\(^{3}\). Find the value of \(x\) for this box, and show that it needs more than 20 % extra card compared with the box in part (e).

idea: The area of a triangle is \(\dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C\). The volume of a prism is the area of its end times its length; use it to remove \(l\), so the card depends on \(x\) only. The box has two triangular ends and three rectangular sides.

solution.label: a
steps: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is \(60^\circ\): area \(= \dfrac{1}{2}x \cdot x \sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}x^{2} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).

solution.label: e
steps: \(\sqrt{3}\,x = \dfrac{6000}{\sqrt{3}\,x^{2}}\), so \(3x^{3} = 6000\) and \(x^{3} = 2000\): \(x = 12.59\ldots\) The gradient goes from negative to positive, so this is a minimum.

solution.label: g
solution.answer: \(x = 7.60\) cm; it needs about 22.7 % more card, which is more than 20 %

stem: Cars arrive at the toll booths of a bridge between 7 am and 9 am. The rate at which they arrive, \(R\) cars per minute, \(t\) minutes after 7 am is modelled by \[R(t) = 20 + 1.5t - 0.0125t^{2}, \quad 0 \le t \le 120.\] The booths can let through at most 50 cars per minute. When cars arrive faster than this, a queue builds up; the queue gets shorter again when they arrive more slowly. There is no queue at 7 am.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down the rate at which cars arrive at 7 am.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find \(R'(t)\), and hence find the time at which cars arrive fastest and the rate at that time.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the total number of cars that arrive between 7 am and 9 am.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Find the two times of day at which cars arrive at exactly 50 per minute. Give your answers to the nearest minute.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Explain why the queue is longest at the second of these times.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the number of cars in the queue at that time.

idea: Integrating a rate gives a total. The queue grows by the amount by which the arrivals exceed 50 per minute, so its length is the area between the graph of \(R\) and the line \(R = 50\), from when the queue starts to grow.

solution.label: b
steps: \(R'(t) = 1.5 - 0.025t\), which is zero at \(t = 60\). \(R'\) is positive before and negative after, so this is a maximum.
solution.answer: \(R'(t) = 1.5 - 0.025t\); fastest at 8 am, 65 cars per minute

solution.label: d
steps: 25 minutes after 7 am is 7:25; 95 minutes after 7 am is 8:35.

solution.label: e
steps: Between the two times, cars arrive faster than they can get through, so the queue keeps growing. After the second time, they arrive more slowly than 50 per minute and the queue shrinks.
solution.answer: The queue grows until \(R\) falls back to 50, then starts to shrink

stem: A patient takes a painkiller. The concentration of the drug in the blood, \(C\) mg per litre, \(t\) hours later changes at a rate \[\frac{\mathrm{d}C}{\mathrm{d}t} = 0.15t^{2} - 2.4t + 7.2, \quad 0 \le t \le 12.\] At \(t = 0\) the concentration is zero.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find an expression for \(C\) in terms of \(t\).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest concentration and the time at which it occurs.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time at which the concentration is falling fastest, and the rate at which it is falling then.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The painkiller works while the concentration is at least 5 mg per litre. Find the length of time for which it works.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Show that at \(t = 12\) the concentration and its rate of change are both zero.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the area under the graph of \(C\) for \(0 \le t \le 12\), and hence find the mean concentration over the 12 hours.

idea: Integrate the rate to get \(C\), using \(C(0) = 0\) for the constant. The greatest value of \(C\) is where the rate is zero; the fastest fall is where the rate itself has its most negative value.

solution.label: b
steps: \(0.15(t^{2} - 16t + 48) = 0.15(t - 4)(t - 12) = 0\), so \(t = 4\) or \(t = 12\). The rate is positive before \(t = 4\) and negative after it.
solution.answer: 12.8 mg per litre, 4 hours after taking it

solution.label: c
steps: The rate \(0.15t^{2} - 2.4t + 7.2\) has its least value where \(0.3t - 2.4 = 0\), at \(t = 8\).
solution.answer: At \(t = 8\) hours, falling at 2.4 mg per litre per hour

solution.label: d
steps: Solve \(0.05t^{3} - 1.2t^{2} + 7.2t = 5\) with the calculator, for \(0 \le t \le 12\): \(t = 0.7967\ldots\) and \(t = 8.587\ldots\)

solution.label: f
solution.answer: Area 86.4; mean concentration 7.2 mg per litre

stem: During a 12-minute storm, rainwater runs off a roof into a tank at a rate of \((6t - 0.5t^{2})\) litres per minute, where \(t\) is the time in minutes since the storm began. At the same time, water runs out of a tap at the bottom of the tank at a constant 8 litres per minute. At \(t = 0\) the tank holds 40 litres. Let \(V\) litres be the volume of water in the tank at time \(t\), for \(0 \le t \le 12\).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write down an expression for \(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}t}\).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the two times at which the volume of water is not changing.

parts.label: d
parts.text: According to the model, find the least and the greatest volume of water in the tank for \(0 \le t \le 12\).

parts.label: e
parts.text: In fact the tank holds only 90 litres. Show that it overflows, and find the time at which it first becomes full.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Find the time at which rain runs into the tank fastest, and the rate at that time.

idea: The rate of change of the volume is the rate in minus the rate out. Integrating it, with the 40 litres at the start, gives \(V\). The volume stops changing when the two rates are equal.

solution.label: d
steps: The rate is negative before \(t = 1.527\ldots\), positive between the two times and negative after: a minimum, then a maximum.

solution.label: e
steps: The greatest volume, 93.8 litres, is more than 90 litres, so the tank overflows.
Solve \(40 - 8t + 3t^{2} - \dfrac{t^{3}}{6} = 90\) with the calculator; the first solution is \(t = 9.093\ldots\)
solution.answer: It first becomes full after 9.09 minutes

solution.label: f
steps: The rate in, \(6t - 0.5t^{2}\), is greatest where \(6 - t = 0\), at \(t = 6\).
